[IBNATIYYA:107:4/r1] IBNATIYYA, d. 542 · author | reports | A report places the revelation among people compelled into Islam in Mecca who were not firm, then succumbed to persecution and treated Muslims harshly; some prayed with them at times out of caution or confusion.

[IBNATIYYA:107:5/r1] IBNATIYYA, d. 542 · author | reports | A report places the revelation among people compelled into Islam in Mecca who were not firm, then succumbed to persecution and treated Muslims harshly; some prayed with them at times out of caution or confusion.

[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p244#2/r1] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | holds | The passage concerns hypocrites who expect reward for praying in the Prophet's presence but do not fear punishment when they skip prayer, so they pray for show when he is there and leave it otherwise. | mentions 107:6
[RAZI:107:4/r1] RAZI, d. 606 · author | holds | The transition from mistreating orphans and withholding food to prayer contrasts dealings with creatures against service to the Creator: prayer without humility is an even clearer sign of hypocrisy.
[RAZI:107:4/r2] RAZI, d. 606 · author | holds | Mention of orphan abuse and failure to urge feeding prompts the question whether prayer prevents wrongdoing; the answer is that ostentation and heedlessness make such prayer itself corrupt.
[RAZI:107:4/r3] RAZI, d. 606 · author | holds | Neglect of compassion toward God’s creatures and neglect of reverence toward God complete the person’s misery, hence the warning.

[RAZI:107:4/r5] RAZI, d. 606 · author | reports | A report says each person in Hell laments according to his crime—status-seeking, tribal zeal, or prayer—so one should say on hearing the verse, “Woe to me if God does not forgive me.”
[RAZI-FULL:v32p106#2/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | reports | One link is that mistreating the orphan and withholding help show hypocrisy, while prayer without humility is an even clearer sign because it concerns service to the Creator.
[RAZI-FULL:v32p106#2/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | reports | Another link answers the objection that prayer restrains indecency: this prayer cannot restrain evil when it consists of ostentation and inattention.
[RAZI-FULL:v32p106#2/r3] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | reports | A third link says orphan abuse neglects compassion for God’s creatures, and heedlessness in prayer neglects reverence for God; failing in both completes wretchedness.
[RAZI-FULL:v32p106#2/r4] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Woe is used for grave crimes, as in warnings against fraud, scribal wrongdoing, and slander. | mentions 83:1, 2:79, 104:1
[RAZI-FULL:v32p106#2/r5] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | reports | A report says each person in Hell wails according to his offense, including love of status, tribal zeal, or prayer; the listener should say, Woe to me unless God forgives me.
[RAZI-FULL:v32p107/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | The threat covers three sins: heedlessness about prayer, ostentation, and withholding small aid; since these do not alone make a Muslim hypocrite, commentators explain why the warning is so severe.
[RAZI-FULL:v32p107/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | prefers | The preferred answer limits the description to hypocritical worshippers: their extra punishment for forbidden acts and omitted duties supports al-Shafi‘i’s view that unbelievers are addressed by the subsidiary laws.
[QURTUBI:107:4/r1] QURTUBI, d. 671 · author | holds | Wayl means punishment; Qurṭubī notes that this has been explained in several earlier passages.
[QURTUBI-FULL:107:1-5/r12] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | The woe announced for the worshippers means punishment.
[BAYDAWI:107:7/r5] BAYDAWI, d. 685 · author | holds | Calling them worshippers rather than using a pronoun highlights their bad treatment of both Creator and creatures.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:107:1-5/r6] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | Woe is for worshippers who are inattentive to their prayers, heedless and unconcerned about them.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:107:6-7/r4] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | The fa in the woe passage is consequential: neglect of the orphan already shows weak religion and deserves blame, so heedlessness of prayer, ostentation, and withholding zakāt merit it even more; prayer is religion's pillar, ostentation a branch of unbelief, and zakāt Islam's bridge.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:107:6-7/r5] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | Alternatively, the fa can mark causation, meaning, “So woe is theirs.”
[BAYDAWI-FULL:107:6-7/r6] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | Calling them “those who pray” in place of a pronoun signals their bad treatment of both the Creator and other people.

[NASAFI:107:4/r3] NASAFI, d. 710 · author | reports | Another description is hypocrites who outwardly count themselves among worshippers but neglect prayer, seek neither nearness nor fulfillment of duty, go through motions mindlessly, display worship, and withhold alms and useful things.

[ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r6] ABUHAYYAN, d. 745 · الزمخشري | reports | Al-Zamakhsharī proposes coordinating fa-dhālika with alladhī yukadhdhib, deleting arayta’s second object and using the following woe as its indication. | mentions 107:1, 107:4
[ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r7] ABUHAYYAN, d. 745 · author | reports | Al-Zamakhsharī reads “woe to the praying” as “woe to them”: their description replaces the pronoun because they deny requital, neglect prayer, show off, and do not purify their wealth. | mentions 107:1, 107:5, 107:6

[ABUHAYYAN:107:4/r4] ABUHAYYAN, d. 745 · author | prefers | The praying people here are, God knows best, hypocrites; their prayer is established only as the outward postures they perform.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p552/r10] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | After naming denial of judgment as the root of unbelief, the passage turns to prayer as worship owed to the Creator.

[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p553/r9] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | rejects | The author calls al-Zamakhsharī's accusative parsing of fa-dhālika strange and unnatural: a nominative subject is immediate, while an accusative would require repeating the verb and pointing needlessly to the person.

[NASHR:v2p203/r1] NASHR, d. 833 · أهل الأداء | reports | Teachers forbid stopping between a genitive annexation and its governing noun; they rejected the defense that such a written break merely marked a hypothetical pause.
[NASHR:v2p203/r2] NASHR, d. 833 · أهل الأداء | reports | The sixth rule requires a reader to finish the second reciter's reading to the end of the verse before restoring anything omitted from the first, avoiding an unmarked splice of two readers.

[BIQAI-FULL:v8p541/r1] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | Al-Māʿūn is also called al-Dīn, Araʾayta and al-Takdhīb; its central warning is that denial of resurrection and recompense is the root of vices and contempt for sacred matters.
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p542/r1] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | Harshness to orphans, failure to encourage feeding the poor, neglect of prayer, ostentation and withholding help all mark denial of judgment; belief instead produces praised conduct, so believers must avoid these traits.
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p543/r1] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | After faults toward people, the text turns to faults toward God: both reveal a ruined heart and invite divine displeasure, showing how destructive sins are.
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p543/r2] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The threat begins with wa'il, the strongest expression of humiliation, then targets people characterized by heedlessness of prayer.
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p543/r3] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The plural 'those who pray' generalizes the warning to the whole class: whoever scorns the weak may neglect what is unseen, and one who abandons prayer is still more careless about other duties.
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p543/r4] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | A description rather than a verb ties the threat to a persistent trait; the intended targets are accountable people liable to prayer, not simply anyone presently performing it.
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p543/r5] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم | reports | A prophetic report says God does not accept the prayer of a menstruating woman unless she wears a head covering, supporting the reference to those obligated to pray.
[DURR:107:4/r1] DURR, d. 911 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn ʿAbbās identifies these inattentive worshippers as hypocrites: they pray for show when seen, leave prayer when alone, and out of spite withhold borrowed goods, which are al-māʿūn.
[DURR-FULL:v8p641/r9] DURR-FULL, d. 911 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn Abbas identifies the inattentive worshippers as hypocrites: they pray ostentatiously in public, abandon prayer in private, and withhold loaned household items; this is al-maʿun.
[ITQAN:v1p227/r3] ITQAN, d. 911 · author | holds | Stopping at “woe to those who pray” is among the most abhorrent stops because the unfinished phrase suggests a false meaning.
[ITQAN:v3p297/r2] ITQAN, d. 911 · author | holds | Al-Kawthar counters al-Ma'un's four traits: abundant giving opposes miserliness, prayer opposes neglect, worship for God opposes showing off, and sacrifice meat is charity opposing withholding small kindnesses. | mentions 108:1, 108:2
[SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p235#2/r1] SUYUTI-LUBAB, d. 911 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn Abbas says the threatened worshippers were hypocrites who performed prayer ostentatiously when believers saw them, abandoned it when unseen, and withheld borrowed household goods.
[BURSEVI:v10p403#2/r2] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | Given their disregard for orphan and poor, the conditional implication is that woe means severe punishment for these worshippers.
[ALUSI:107:4/r1] ALUSI, d. 1270 · author | holds | The threat concerns worshippers indifferent to prayer: they may omit it altogether or let its time expire.
[ALUSI:107:5/r1] ALUSI, d. 1270 · author | holds | The threat concerns worshippers indifferent to prayer: they may omit it altogether or let its time expire.
[ALUSI:107:7/r11] ALUSI, d. 1270 · author | holds | The fāʾ in fa-wayl is consequential: the discourse escalates from orphan-pushing to prayer-neglect, ostentation, and withholding zakāt or customary loans, increasingly exposing denial of religion.
[ALUSI:107:7/r16] ALUSI, d. 1270 · صاحب الكشف | reports | The Kashf author says that if the orphan-pusher is a named individual, treating the later prayer-neglect and ostentation as further identifying labels is ill-fitting; those clauses work as a digression prompted by the orphan-pushing description.
[ALUSI:107:7/r17] ALUSI, d. 1270 · author | holds | Al-Ālūsī says the sūra's main concern is denial of religion, using orphan-abuse as its identifying sign and the later vices to press the question whether such conduct is good or evil, like the rebuke in 5:91. | mentions 5:91
[ALUSI:107:7/r18] ALUSI, d. 1270 · بعضهم | reports | Some make the fāʾ causal from the preceding coordination, requiring the worshippers and deniers to be one group; they are then identified as hypocrites, a reading reported from Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, and Mālik, and supported by the ostentation clause.
[ALUSI:107:7/r19] ALUSI, d. 1270 · ابن عباس ومجاهد والإمام مالك | reports | Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, and Imām Mālik are reported to identify the worshippers as hypocrites; al-Baḥr cites the ostentation description as evidence.
[ALUSI:107:7/r20] ALUSI, d. 1270 · قيل | reports | On the unified-group reading, the worshippers could be all legally accountable people, even non-hypocrite disbelievers, and heedlessness could mean total abandonment of prayer, entailing that disbelievers are obligated by legal branches.
